description: The NCI-60 Human Tumor Cell Line Screen is a free resource offered by the National Cancer Institute's Developmental Therapeutics Program (DTP). It assesses the anti-cancer activity of small molecules and natural products across a diverse panel of 60 human tumor cell lines. The platform currently operates using the HTS384 format: a high-throughput, 384-well plate assay with a sensitive CellTiter-Glo luminescent readout. This modernized version increases speed, throughput, and data precision while maintaining consistency with decades of historical screening results.

description: Mislabeling of the SW-1271 and NCI-H2066 SCLC lines was discovered after the molecular and drug response measures had been recorded. The correct identity of both cell lines has been confirmed using DNA fingerprinting and analytical tools. The December 2019 release of the SCLC dataset includes corrected labeling of the cell lines. The December 2019 release provides corrected labeling for these two cell lines in all files for all measures of drug response, transcript expression, miRNA expression. The mislabeling was discovered before the methylation studies; so, all of the DNA methylation datasets have correct designations of the SW-1271 and NCI-H2066 lines.

description: The NPNPD was created to accelerate drug discovery. It is high-throughput amenable library comprising plant, marine and microbial biota from around the world. The Natural Products Branch (NPB) works with collaborators to provide natural product expertise in high-throughput screening. Depending on the level of collaboration, the NPB can provide faster analytical resources (isolation, structure elucidation, and resupply) to expedite translational pipelines. The NCI is committed to the conservation of biological diversity and fair and equitable collaboration and compensation with the source countries.

description: NCI's Proteomic Data Commons (PDC) is part of the NCI's Cancer Research Data Commons (CRDC) data ecosystem. description: Altered DNA methylation patterns play important roles in cancer development and progression. We examined whether expression levels of genes directly or indirectly involved in DNA methylation and demethylation may be associated with response of cancer cell lines to chemotherapy treatment comprising a variety of antitumor agents. We analyzed 72 genes encoding epigenetic factors directly or indirectly involved in DNA methylation and demethylation processes. We analyzed data from 645 cancer cell lines and 23 cancer types from the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia and Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer datasets. We observed numerous correlations between expression of genes encoding epigenetic factors and response to chemotherapeutic agents.

dataset_title: History of the NCI-60 screen and COMPARE algorithm
description: The COMPARE algorithm is a powerful tool developed by NCI to help researchers explore and interpret patterns of compound activity in the NCI-60 Human Tumor Cell Line Screen. By comparing a compound's activity fingerprint across the 60 cell lines to historical and contemporary data, COMPARE predicts potential mechanisms of action, tumor selectivity, and chemical analogs. COMPARE has been an integral part of drug discovery at NCI for over 30 years and continues to evolve with the new HTS384 screen.
